title: Trace formula over a finite extension
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, and the
coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with
$A_n=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$. Let $X_0$ be
separated finite-type
over $k_0$ ([def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]), put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, let
$K_E\in D^b_c(X,E)$ be an object of the
rationalized
$E$-coefficient category ([def-weil-rationalization-karoubi],
[def-weil-pbc-rational-category]), and let

$$
\varphi_E:Lg_\gamma^*K_E\longrightarrow K_E
$$

be an arbitrary morphism of $D^b_c(X,E)$, for instance the Weil
structure of an $E$-Weil complex. No invertibility of $\varphi_E$, no
invertibility of a rescaling $c\,\varphi_E$ on a lattice, and no
integral Weil presentation is assumed. Let $F^{\,m}_{c,K_E}$ on
$R\Gamma_c(X,K_E)$ and $F_{y,m}$ on $K_{E,\bar y}$ be the $E$-stage
Frobenius operators of $(K_E,\varphi_E)$ defined in
[prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model] (the stalk being
$K_{\mathcal O,\bar y}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ for a lattice
$K_{\mathcal O}$, as there).

*Lattice and finite-level hypotheses.* Let $K_{\mathcal O}\in
D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ ([def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed])
together with an isomorphism $\alpha:K_{\mathcal O}\xrightarrow{\sim}K_E$
of $D^b_c(X,E)$ be a lattice of $K_E$. One always exists: the objects of
$D^b_c(X,E)$ are those of $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$, so one may take
$K_{\mathcal O}=K_E$ and $\alpha=\operatorname{id}$. Put
$K_n=K_{\mathcal O}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n$. Assume at every finite
level $n$ the finite-level hypotheses of
[thm-trf-coefficient-morphism-trace-formula] for $K_n$. These are an
explicit etale-origin witness for $K_n$
([def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]) and the exceptional-adjoint
admissibility of [def-trf-admissibility] for the graph correspondences of
the iterates $\Phi^m$ and the fixed-point base changes on a chosen
compactification defined over $k_0$. They concern $K_n$ and the geometry
of $X_0$ only, not $\varphi_E$; they are the data "assumed at each
finite level" in the source and are not proved here.

Then the $E$-vector spaces $H_c^i(X,K_E)$ and $H^j(K_{E,\bar y})$ are
finite-dimensional and nonzero for only finitely many $i$, $j$, and for
every $m\geq1$,

$$
\sum_{i\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^i
\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F_{c,K_E}^m\mid H_c^i(X,K_E)\bigr)
=
\sum_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}
\sum_{j\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^j
\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F_{y,m}\mid H^j(K_{E,\bar y})\bigr)
$$

in $E$. For any clearing of denominators $\varphi_E=\varpi^{-N}u$ on the
lattice, the two sides are $\varpi^{-Nm}$ times the images under
$\mathcal O_E\to E$ of the two sides of the integral identity of
[thm-trf-integral-adic-coefficient-morphism-trace-formula], item (2), and
they agree with the corresponding $E$-valued categorical traces by the
supertrace law over the field $E$ of [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws].

This covers the Weil structure of every $E$-Weil complex. It also covers
Weil maps that are not invertible after any rescaling on any lattice, such
as $\varphi_E=\operatorname{diag}(1,\ell)$ on $E^2$ over
$X_0=\Spec\mathbf F_q$ (the example of
[prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model]). The earlier hypothesis of a
strict integral Weil presentation of some rescaling $c\,\varphi_E$ is a
special case and is no longer needed.

proof.text: Reduction tower. Put $R=\mathcal O_E$ and $\varpi=\varpi_E$. By [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the reductions $K_n$ are bounded constructible and have cohomology in a common interval $[r,s]$. Apply [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] to $K_{\mathcal O}$: its residue reduction $K_1$ has cohomology in $[r,s]$, so every $K_n$ has Tor amplitude in $[r,s]$. The hypothesis that $\ell$ is invertible on $X$ holds because $X$ has characteristic $p\ne\ell$. Thus $K_n\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$. The functorial reduction tower and its quotient normalization isomorphisms, including their naturality and cocycle, are supplied by [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], applied to $R$ and $(\varpi)$. By [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], $R$ is a DVR (hence Noetherian) and the quotients $A_n$ are finite. The finite residue field $A_1$ is additively torsion. Since $\varpi^n$ is nonzero in the domain $R$, the complex $[R\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}R]$ in degrees $-1,0$ is a finite free resolution of $A_n$, so the perfect-quotient hypothesis of that datum holds. Hence the tower is normalized in the sense of [def-trf-adic-system]. No Weil structure is needed for this normalized tower.

Transport to the chosen lattice. In the rationalized category set $\widetilde\varphi=\alpha^{-1}\varphi_E Lg_\gamma^*\alpha$. The exact $E$-linear extensions and natural transformations of [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] apply to the operations specified in [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model]. Write $G=Lg_\gamma^*$ and use its supplied composition isomorphisms to identify $G^m=Lg_\gamma^{m*}$. The formula $\widetilde\varphi^{[1]}=\alpha^{-1}\varphi_E G\alpha$ is the definition. If $\widetilde\varphi^{[m]}=\alpha^{-1}\varphi_E^{[m]}G^m\alpha$, then
$$\widetilde\varphi^{[m+1]}=\widetilde\varphi^{[m]}G^m(\widetilde\varphi)=\alpha^{-1}\varphi_E^{[m]}G^m\alpha\,G^m(\alpha^{-1})G^m(\varphi_E)G^{m+1}\alpha=\alpha^{-1}\varphi_E^{[m+1]}G^{m+1}\alpha.$$
Here $G^m\alpha\,G^m(\alpha^{-1})=1$. Let $C=R\Gamma_c(X,-)$ and $T=(-)_{\bar y}$. Naturality gives $C(G^m\alpha)g_{\gamma,c,K_{\mathcal O}}^{m,*}=g_{\gamma,c,K_E}^{m,*}C(\alpha)$ and $T(G^m\alpha)\tau_{y,m,K_{\mathcal O}}=\tau_{y,m,K_E}T(\alpha)$. Substitution in the defining operator formulas yields $\widetilde F_{c,m}=C(\alpha)^{-1}F_{c,K_E}^{m}C(\alpha)$ and $\widetilde F_{y,m}=T(\alpha)^{-1}F_{y,m}T(\alpha)$. The conjugating maps $C(\alpha)$ and $T(\alpha)$ are isomorphisms. Once finiteness is established in Step 4, ordinary traces are unchanged: matrices in bases transported by these isomorphisms are identical. It suffices to prove the assertion for $K_E$ represented by $K_{\mathcal O}$ with $\alpha=1$ and morphism $\widetilde\varphi$.

Clear denominators without imposing invertibility. Apply [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model] to the integral lattice with normalized reduction tower from Step 1 and the transported rational morphism from Step 2. Its item (1) gives $N\geq0$ and $u:Lg_\gamma^*K_{\mathcal O}\to K_{\mathcal O}$ with $\widetilde\varphi=\varpi^{-N}u$. Its item (2) gives compatible coefficient morphisms $\psi_n=u_n\kappa_{K_n}$ and identifies their iterates. Its items (3) and (4) give integral operators $U_m,U_{y,m}$, reducing to the finite-level global and stalk operators, together with
$$F_{c,K_E}^{\,m}=\varpi^{-Nm}(U_m\otimes_R E),\qquad F_{y,m}=\varpi^{-Nm}(U_{y,m}\otimes_R E).$$
These assertions allow arbitrary coefficient morphisms; $u$ and its reductions need not be isomorphisms.

source.place: Step 2: the integral model, clearing denominators and operators

proof.text: Perfect realization and finiteness. Apply item (2) of [prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems] to the normalized tower of Step 1 and the compatible morphisms of Step 3. It gives bounded finite free $R$-complexes representing $P=R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})$ and $P_y=K_{\mathcal O,\bar y}$; its statement explicitly identifies these with the compact-support and completed-stalk realizations for a reduction tower. Rational compact support is the scalar extension of $P$ by [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]; the rational stalk is the scalar extension of $P_y$ by [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model]. For clarity that these extensions can be computed on the finite free representatives: free modules tensor exactly (tensoring with $R^d$ is a finite direct sum), so [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] makes these bounded complexes K-flat, and [lem-pc-kflat-scalar-extension-counit] identifies their derived scalar extensions naturally with termwise extension along $R\to E$. The resulting terms are finite-dimensional $E$-vector spaces and vanish outside finitely many degrees. Each cohomology is a subquotient of such a term, proving the asserted finite-dimensionality and boundedness, also for the original object by Step 2.

source.place: Step 2: bounded finite free integral realizations and finiteness

proof.text:
Integral trace identity. The normalized tower of Step 1 and the compatible maps of Step 3 satisfy the hypotheses of [thm-trf-integral-adic-coefficient-morphism-trace-formula]. Its finite-level etale-origin witnesses and exceptional-adjoint admissibility on the chosen compactification are exactly the hypotheses retained in the present statement; they concern the objects and geometry and require no inverse for $\psi_n$. Its lattice form, item (2), therefore gives for every $m\geq1$
$$\operatorname{tr}_R(U_m\mid P)=\sum_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}\operatorname{tr}_R(U_{y,m}\mid P_y).$$

Scalar extension of the integral traces. For either $(P,U)=(P,U_m)$ or $(P_y,U_{y,m})$, choose the bounded finite free model $M$ of Step 4. By [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative], transport of $U$ to $M$ is represented by a chain endomorphism $v$; its source is bounded above, and each finite free term is projective: a map from it through a surjection lifts by choosing a preimage for the image of each basis vector. Thus the cited lemma applies. The natural counit isomorphism of [lem-pc-kflat-scalar-extension-counit] identifies the extension of this morphism with $v\otimes_R E$ on $M\otimes_R E$. Write $\rho:R\to E$. Apply [lem-trf-chain-supertrace] over the commutative rings $R$ and $E$ to these two finite free complexes. In each degree the matrix of $v^i\otimes_R E$ is obtained by applying $\rho$ entrywise to the matrix of $v^i$. Since trace is the sum of its diagonal entries, one obtains
$$\rho(\operatorname{tr}_R(U\mid P))=\rho\Bigl(\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(v^i)\Bigr)=\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(v^i\otimes_R E)=\operatorname{tr}_E(U\otimes_R E\mid P\otimes_R E).$$
All sums are finite by boundedness. This proves the required $R\to E$ trace compatibility directly; it does not extend the finite-coefficient scope of the finite-coefficient scalar-extension law by assumption.

Supertraces and the final equality. By the field supertrace law, item (4) of [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws], the $E$-categorical traces in Step 6 are the alternating ordinary traces on cohomology. The scaling formulas of [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model] and Step 3 therefore give
$$\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(F_{c,K_E}^{\,m}\mid H_c^i(X,K_E))=\varpi^{-Nm}\rho(\operatorname{tr}_R(U_m\mid P)),$$
and, for each $y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$,
$$\sum_j(-1)^j\operatorname{Tr}(F_{y,m}\mid H^j(K_{E,\bar y}))=\varpi^{-Nm}\rho(\operatorname{tr}_R(U_{y,m}\mid P_y)).$$ Here scalar multiplication descends to cycles modulo boundaries, and on finite-dimensional cohomology trace scales because it is the sum of diagonal matrix entries. By [lem-weil-point-counts-finite], applied to the finite-type $k_0$-scheme $X_0$ and the finite extension $\mathbf F_{q^m}/k_0$, the set indexing the local sum is finite. Apply the additive homomorphism $\rho$ to Step 5 and multiply by $\varpi^{-Nm}$; substitution gives the required identity, including its categorical-trace interpretation and its asserted expression for any choice $(N,u)$. Any such choice satisfies the same intrinsic formulas of [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model], so the result is independent of the clearing of denominators. Its final example also applies: if $c\operatorname{diag}(1,\ell)$ preserved a lattice invertibly, both eigenvalues $c$ and $c\ell$ would be units, whereas their valuations differ by the positive valuation of $\ell$. This is impossible. Nothing in Steps 1–6 assumes an invertible integral lift, so every Weil isomorphism, and also this example and noninvertible rational maps, are covered.

source.place: Step 4: field supertrace, scaling, finite sum and independence

proof.text:
*Step 0: the reduction tower.* By
[def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] each $K_n$ lies in
$D^b_c(X,A_n)$, and the cohomological supports
([def-weil-cohomological-support]) of all $K_n$ lie in one interval
$[r,s]$. Each $K_n$ has Tor amplitude in $[r,s]$, hence lies in
$D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$. Indeed, let $N$ be an $A_n$-module. The subquotients
$N'$ of the finite filtration $\varpi^iN$ are $A_1$-modules, and
$K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}N'\cong(K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_1)\otimes^L_{A_1}N'
\cong K_1\otimes_{A_1}N'$ by associativity of the derived tensor product
($K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_1\cong K_{\mathcal O}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_1=K_1$).
Since $A_1$ is a field, $N'$ is free, so this is a direct sum of copies of
$K_1$, with cohomology sheaves in degrees $[r,s]$. The distinguished
triangles of the filtration give the same bound for
$K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}N$. The associativity isomorphisms
$K_{n}\otimes^L_{A_{n}}A_j\cong K_j$ ($j\leq n$) and the transitions of the
functorial reduction tower of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] make
$K_\bullet$ a normalized $A_\bullet$-system of [def-trf-adic-system]. In
particular $K_{\mathcal O}$ satisfies the hypotheses of
[prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model].

*Step 1: reduction to $\alpha=\operatorname{id}$.* Put
$\varphi_{\mathcal O}=\alpha^{-1}\circ\varphi_E\circ Lg_\gamma^*\alpha:
Lg_\gamma^*K_{\mathcal O}\to K_{\mathcal O}$ in $D^b_c(X,E)$. By induction
on $m$ and functoriality of the rationalized pullbacks,
$\varphi_{\mathcal O}^{[m]}=\alpha^{-1}\circ\varphi_E^{[m]}\circ
Lg_\gamma^{m*}\alpha$. The base-change isomorphisms $g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$ and
the stalk transports $\tau_{y,m}$ at the stage $E$ are rationalizations of
natural integral transformations ([prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]),
hence natural. So the operators of
[prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model] for
$(K_{\mathcal O},\varphi_{\mathcal O})$ are
$R\Gamma_c(X,\alpha)^{-1}\circ F^{\,m}_{c,K_E}\circ R\Gamma_c(X,\alpha)$ and
$\alpha_{\bar y}^{-1}\circ F_{y,m}\circ\alpha_{\bar y}$. Passing to
cohomology, these are conjugate to the operators for
$(K_E,\varphi_E)$ by $E$-linear isomorphisms, which changes neither the
dimensions nor the traces. We may therefore assume $K_E=K_{\mathcal O}$
(viewed in $D^b_c(X,E)$) and $\alpha=\operatorname{id}$.

*Step 2: the integral model.* By
[prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model], item (1), choose $N\geq0$ and
an integral $u:Lg_\gamma^*K_{\mathcal O}\to K_{\mathcal O}$ with
$\varphi_E=\varpi^{-N}u$. By its item (2), $\psi_n=u_n\circ\kappa_{K_n}$ is a
compatible system of Frobenius coefficient morphisms on $K_\bullet$, not
necessarily invertible. By its items (3) and (4), the integral operators
$U_m$ on $R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})$ and $U_{y,m}$ on
$K_{\mathcal O,\bar y}$ satisfy

$$
F^{\,m}_{c,K_E}=\varpi^{-Nm}\bigl(U_m\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E\bigr),
\qquad
F_{y,m}=\varpi^{-Nm}\bigl(U_{y,m}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E\bigr).
$$

By item (2) of [prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems], applied to
the reduction tower $K_\bullet$ (for which
$P_{\mathcal O}=R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})$ and
$P_{\bar y,\mathcal O}=K_{\mathcal O,\bar y}$), both complexes are
represented by bounded complexes of finite free $\mathcal O_E$-modules.
Hence $R\Gamma_c(X,K_E)=R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$
([def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]) and
$K_{E,\bar y}=K_{\mathcal O,\bar y}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ are bounded
complexes of finite-dimensional $E$-vector spaces, which is the finiteness
assertion.

*Step 3: the integral identity.* The finite-level hypotheses assumed in the
statement are those of
[thm-trf-integral-adic-coefficient-morphism-trace-formula] for
$(K_\bullet,\psi_\bullet)$: they do not involve $\psi_n$. Its item (2)
gives

$$
\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}\bigl(U_m\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})\bigr)
=\sum_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}
\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}\bigl(U_{y,m}\mid K_{\mathcal O,\bar y}\bigr)
\quad\text{in }\mathcal O_E .
$$

*Step 4: rationalization.* Let $\rho:\mathcal O_E\to E$ be the inclusion.
Since $E$ is flat over $\mathcal O_E$, $P\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}E=P\otimes
_{\mathcal O_E}E$ for the complexes of Step 2, and the scalar-extension law
of [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws], item (3), gives
$\rho\bigl(\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}(U_m)\bigr)
=\operatorname{tr}_E\bigl(U_m\otimes E\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K_E)\bigr)$, and
likewise for each $U_{y,m}$ (directly: by the chain-level computation of
[lem-trf-chain-supertrace] over $\mathcal O_E$ and over $E$, both sides
equal $\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(U_m^i\mid M^i)$ for a finite free
model $M$ of Step 2 and a chain representative of $U_m$). By the
supertrace law over the field $E$,
item (4) of the same proposition,
$\operatorname{tr}_E(U_m\otimes E)=\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}
\bigl(H^i(U_m\otimes E)\mid H_c^i(X,K_E)\bigr)$, and likewise for the stalks.
The cohomology functors $H^i$ are $E$-linear on morphisms and the ordinary
trace is $E$-linear, so by Step 2

$$
\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F^{\,m}_{c,K_E}\mid H_c^i(X,K_E)\bigr)
=\varpi^{-Nm}\rho\Bigl(\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}\bigl(U_m\mid
R\Gamma_c(X,K_{\mathcal O})\bigr)\Bigr),
$$

and likewise
$\sum_j(-1)^j\operatorname{Tr}(F_{y,m}\mid H^j(K_{E,\bar y}))
=\varpi^{-Nm}\rho\bigl(\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}(U_{y,m}\mid
K_{\mathcal O,\bar y})\bigr)$. The set $X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ is finite
($X_0$ is of finite type over $k_0$) and $\rho$ is additive. Applying $\rho$
to the identity of Step 3 and multiplying by $\varpi^{-Nm}$ gives the
displayed identity. The result does not depend on the choice of $(N,u)$:
replacing it by $(N+1,\varpi u)$ multiplies $U_m$, $U_{y,m}$ by $\varpi^m$
and leaves $\varpi^{-Nm}(U_m\otimes E)$ unchanged
([prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model]).
